answer: Each agent gets an identity-bound stake that is locked before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. A verifier samples its work and can slash that stake when the agent submits provably duplicated or invalid results; honest agents can challenge with evidence and share the forfeiture. Splitting one operator across a nebula of aliases does not multiply trust: every alias needs separately locked capital, and each can lose it. The attacker pays real funds and risks them across the horizon of the challenge window, while the atlas of identities makes shared control easier to detect.
